title: India Gold Demand Seen At Six-Year Low As Prices Weigh
excerpt: The World Gold Council estimates India's 2026 demand will fall to around 650 metric tons, after September-quarter demand dropped 29% year-on-year to 162.5 tons.
body:
• The World Gold Council estimates India's total gold demand in 2026 will fall to around 650 metric tons, the lowest since 2020 — this is a WGC estimate and outlook, not a final result.
  • India's gold demand fell 29% year-on-year to 162.5 metric tons in the September quarter, with jewellery purchases down 20% and investment demand down 40%, according to the WGC's India chief cited by Reuters.
  • Elevated prices, rising living costs and a weak monsoon that curbed rural incomes are the main drags cited by the WGC.
  • Globally, the WGC cut its forecast for growth in gold investment demand this year to 200 tons from 400 tons, while raising its central bank buying estimate.

India's gold demand is expected to fall to a six-year low in 2026 as elevated prices weigh on jewellery sales and investment demand moderates, the World Gold Council said on Tuesday, in an estimate reported by Reuters.

Jewellery demand fell in the first nine months of the year, which will drag total demand down to around 650 metric tons, the lowest since 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic forced jewellery shops to close, Sachin Jain, chief executive of the WGC's Indian operations, told Reuters. That 650-ton figure is the WGC's outlook for the full year, not a recorded final total.

India is the world's biggest gold consumer after China, Reuters noted. The country is grappling with rising living costs in the wake of the Iran war, while a weak monsoon could curtail rural demand for jewellery, the report said.

What the September quarter showed

Gold demand fell 29% year-on-year to 162.5 metric tons in the September quarter, as jewellery purchases declined 20% and investment demand dropped 40%, Jain said, according to Reuters.

Demand is likely to improve in the December quarter as festivals such as Diwali and the wedding season drive purchases, Jain said. Indians celebrated Dussehra in October and will celebrate Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious, Reuters reported. But high prices and weakness in the rural economy following a poor monsoon are likely to cap demand, the WGC said in its report published on Tuesday.

More than half of India's gold demand comes from rural areas, where jewellery is a traditional store of wealth for millions, Reuters said. The monsoon delivered its lowest rainfall in more than a decade in 2026, curbing agricultural production and reducing farmers' incomes, according to the report.

India's gold imports also fell in the September quarter, partly due to a rise in unofficial inflows after the government raised import duties on the precious metal earlier this year, Jain told Reuters.

The global picture behind the India estimate

The India outlook sits inside a softer global investment picture. In a separate Reuters report on the WGC's quarterly demand trends, the council cut its forecast for growth in gold investment this year to 200 metric tons from 400 tons previously, citing weaker appetite for bars and coins, although it raised its estimate for central bank purchases.

"While demand from gold ETFs has exceeded expectations, bar and coin demand, although still relatively resilient, slowed notably in the second half of 2026," the WGC said in that report.

Spot gold, which hit a one-year low on Friday, has fallen 29% since reaching a record high of $5,595 an ounce in January, Reuters reported, as the Iran war boosted oil prices and fuelled expectations of higher interest rates. Physically backed gold exchange-traded funds recorded inflows of 211 tons in the third quarter, while bar and coin demand dropped 19% year-on-year to 268 tons and jewellery consumption fell 17% to 313 tons, the weakest third quarter since the data series began in 2000, according to the WGC figures cited by Reuters.

Central banks moved the other way. Purchases, including reported and estimated buying, rose 42% to 321 tons, the highest quarterly total since the fourth quarter of 2024, lifting year-to-date net purchases to 675 tons, Reuters reported. The WGC now expects central bank purchases to at least match the 848 tons bought in 2025.

For India, the distinction matters for readers: the September-quarter decline is reported data cited by the WGC, while the roughly 650-ton full-year figure and the six-year-low ranking are the council's estimate, dependent on how strongly Diwali, wedding-season and rural demand recover in the final quarter.
